discrepancies.summary: Batch Error Continuation wording
alternatives: Continue means later batch items proceed without rollback, as its first description states.
Continue also undoes completed items and returns Undone statuses, as the following description states.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Batch ordering, rollback expectations, result status handling, and client-side interpretation.

discrepancies.summary: HTTPS encoding declarations conflict with a binary TTLV HTTP body requirement
alternatives: The body uses the selected TTLV, XML, or JSON encoding indicated by Content-Type.
The body is binary TTLV regardless of the listed XML and JSON Content-Type cases.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: HTTPS request and response codecs, Content-Type selection, and the TTLV-only 1.0 boundary.

discrepancies.summary: Baseline conformance points to a second mandatory test suite

discrepancies.downstream_impact: Baseline profile test obligations and the exact evidence set.

discrepancies.downstream_impact: Scope of permitted extra clauses in the XML Client profile.

discrepancies.summary: XML Server MAY clause points to the JSON Server section
alternatives: The conflict boundary refers to XML Server §5.4.3.

discrepancies.downstream_impact: Scope of permitted extra clauses in the XML Server profile.

discrepancies.summary: AES XTS Client MAY clause points to Opaque Managed Object Client

discrepancies.downstream_impact: Scope of optional additions permitted by the AES XTS Client profile.

discrepancies.summary: PKCS#11 Client MAY clause points to JSON Client
alternatives: The conflict boundary refers to PKCS#11 Client §5.18.3.
The printed JSON Client §5.5.2 reference is intentional.
discrepancies.downstream_impact: Scope of optional additions permitted by the PKCS#11 Client profile.

discrepancies.summary: PKCS#11 Server MAY clause points to JSON Server

alternatives: MAY NOT is intended as a prohibition.
MAY NOT is intended as permission with a negated condition or another noncanonical meaning.
